title: OpenStax says babies babble in repeated syllables, alone as well as with someone
summary: OpenStax Psychology says that in the babbling stage babies repeat syllables, and that they babble alone as well as with caregivers.
body: OpenStax Psychology, section 7.2, says that after the first few months babies enter a babbling stage and tend to produce single syllables repeated over and over, with more variety as time passes. It says it is unlikely they are trying to communicate in that stage, because they are just as likely to babble when alone as when a caregiver is there. The section cites Fernandez and Cairns, 2011, for that point. This card reports the textbook's statement. It is not a CDC milestone age, and the first-edition web view is CC BY 4.0.
